transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (CTO, Silverpine), Mark Dalton (Head of Infra, Silverpine), Lena Ortiz (Security Lead, Silverpine)

Auto-summary (auto): quick discovery on private hosting and network requirements; compliance checks; pilot ask

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE on the account together with Samira our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Rao: good, thanks. aim to keep this tight, we want to understand private deployment options, mainly VPC peering or PrivateLink, curious about cross-account constraints.
[00:17] Samira Khan: great, Priya. quick agenda: we'll ask about your infra, regions, data residency, security, then surface options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), network patterns, and end with next steps. sound ok?
[00:26] Mark Dalton: yep sounds good. quick context: Silverpine is moving inference into production for clinical document summarization. sensitive data, must stay in our VPCs, SOC2 required, and our infra spans us-east-1 and eu-west-1. primary traffic will originate from services in us-east-1.
[00:41] Jordan Lee: perfect. couple clarifying q's — do you want Redwood to run in your VPC (private deployment) or allow private connectivity to Redwood hosted via endpoints?
[00:50] Dr. Priya Rao: we prefer deployment inside our account or at least in a peered VPC under our control. vendor wants no internet egress for PHI.
[00:59] Samira Khan: understood. so two common patterns: 1) Private deployment where Redwood control plane is in a customer VPC or we install a private control plane and inference nodes in your account - full isolation; 2) PrivateLink / Private endpoints into our hosted control plane — less ops but still private connectivity. both have tradeoffs for ops and latency.
[01:20] Mark Dalton: can you clarify the peering vs PrivateLink differences? like cross-account routing and DNS?
[01:25] Samira Khan: sure — VPC peering is direct L3 routing between VPCs, simple, but doesn't support transitive routing, you need route table entries, and for cross-account peering we'll ask for account IDs and CIDRs. PrivateLink (AWS NLB + endpoints) creates ENIs in your VPC and uses interface endpoints — it avoids exposing IPs and can be easier for multi-region. PrivateLink also plays nicer with endpoint policies and security.
[01:46] Dr. Priya Rao: we have existing peering between our ci/prod accounts, but security wants to avoid too many peering relationships. we like private endpoints conceptually. any known limitations?
[01:55] Samira Khan: limitation is you need endpoint capacity per AZ and there's cross-AZ pricing; also some legacy tooling needs specific IP ranges. and DNS is typically handled via Private DNS — you can set up private hosted zones. for large throughput inference, we also consider path MTU and keepalive settings but generally fine.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: also for model weights and artifacts we usually store snapshots on S3 or object storage; if you're running in your VPC we can integrate with your S3 via VPC endpoints. any requirements there?
[02:22] Mark Dalton: yes, S3 gateway endpoints are already in place for prod. we will need Redwood nodes to access our S3 buckets and KMS keys. KMS integration is critical — keys must be customer-managed and HSM-backed where possible.
[02:34] Samira Khan: we support customer KMS for encryption at rest and can integrate with your KMS; for HSMs we can discuss HSM-backed keys or use BYOK patterns. note: some private setups route logs back to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver — we can ship logs to your logging account via cross-account role.
[02:50] Lena Ortiz: about audit logging and retention: we need audit logs retained for 1 year and immutable if possible. also SSO via SAML, SCIM for provisioning.
[02:59] Jordan Lee: Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. retention and exports can be configured; for private deployments we usually ship audit logs to customer-managed S3/Logging.
[03:10] Mark Dalton: what about network egress? we can't allow internet outbound for inference nodes.
[03:15] Samira Khan: if nodes are in your VPC, they don't need outbound internet; any egress (for model pulls or telemetry) can use your NAT or go through VPC endpoints. For hosted PrivateLink path, some control-plane calls might still route through Redwood-managed infra — we can restrict telemetry and disable external telemetry if required.
[03:33] Dr. Priya Rao: latency is a concern — some models need low-10s ms. our primary users are within us-east-1. can you pin inference nodes to us-east-1?
[03:41] Samira Khan: absolutely; we can provision nodes in specific regions. for low latency we'll colocate in us-east-1 and recommend avoiding cross-region calls. if you have eu-west-1 traffic we can provision a second cluster regionally and route requests based on source.
[03:55] Mark Dalton: inter-region replication of KV cache — how does Redwood handle KV cache consistency across regions?
[04:01] Samira Khan: good q — the runtime keeps KV cache per instance; for cross-region consistency we recommend either model routing to local cluster or using a replicated cache layer (customer-managed) if you need shared warm cache. otherwise you accept cache warmup cost on region failover.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: quick risk/ops note — cross-account peering requires changes to route tables and potential security approvals; PrivateLink avoids adding peering relationships but requires endpoint policy config and NLBs.
[04:30] Lena Ortiz: are there IP allowlist requirements for your side? we sometimes need to know static IP ranges to allow through our firewall for control-plane calls.
[04:37] Samira Khan: for PrivateLink you won't need to allow external IPs, but for managed hosted APIs we publish egress IP ranges; for Private deployment in your account there's no outbound to Redwood. If you do dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated VPC) we can provide static egress IP ranges per cluster.
[04:55] Mark Dalton: ok. about bootstrapping and provisioning — how long to spin up a private cluster?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: for private in-customer-account deployments, initial setup with infra changes typically takes 2-4 weeks (depending on approvals); Dedicated reserved clusters in Redwood VPCs can be quicker, ~1-2 weeks after infra prep. pilot can be fast-tracked.
[05:12] Dr. Priya Rao: our timeline — want pilot in Q2, ideally March. success criteria: latency under 150ms 95th for our summarization calls, privacy/no internet egress, and SOC2 controls satisfied.
[05:25] Samira Khan: that aligns with typical pilots. we'll size a 3-node GPU cluster for the pilot and run benchmarks with your payload.
[05:33] Mark Dalton: what about firewall and port requirements?
[05:36] Samira Khan: typically we need outbound HTTPS for control-plane in some modes; for in-account nodes, we only use intra-VPC ports. if you run PrivateLink, we recommend port 443 and the endpoint interface. We can provide a firewall checklist doc.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: i'll add that to the follow-up doc.
[05:53] Lena Ortiz: encryption in transit, TLS, mTLS?
[05:56] Samira Khan: TLS is default. For extra security we support mTLS and mutual auth for service-to-service connections; for private deployments we can configure mTLS with certs managed by your PKI.
[06:08] Dr. Priya Rao: can we bring our own images or do you run your base containers?
[06:12] Samira Khan: typically Redwood runs the inference runtime images we maintain; for private/on-prem there's an option for a customer-approved image build and signing process — we can discuss a hardened image path.
[06:24] Mark Dalton: any constraints around subnet sizing and ENIs? we have limited /20 spaces in prod.
[06:29] Samira Khan: we usually ask for dedicated subnets per AZ and estimate ENI counts based on node sizes. we can do smaller instance density if CIDR is tight, but we'd need to work through the numbers.
[06:41] Jordan Lee: another common ask: DNS resolution — PrivateLink + Private DNS can map api.redwood.example to internal ENIs; for peering you'd use internal IPs. we'll include DNS guidance.
[06:54] Dr. Priya Rao: if we go with PrivateLink, will there be any PII hitting Redwood-managed control plane?
[07:00] Samira Khan: control plane touches metadata; inference payload typically stays in your cluster if nodes run in your account. If you use Redwood hosted inference via PrivateLink, payload still goes to Redwood's service but over private network — we can discuss redaction or tokenization patterns. for full data residency you want nodes in your VPC.
[07:19] Mark Dalton: compliance — you mentioned SOC2 and ISO earlier. do you have cert docs we can share with security?
[07:25] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll attach our SOC2 type II report, ISO27001 cert, and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: we also require vulnerability scanning reports and a penetration test summary annually.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: noted, we'll include recent pen test summary and vuln scan cadence.
[07:44] Dr. Priya Rao: curious about backup and disaster recovery for model artifacts.
[07:49] Samira Khan: model artifacts are stored in S3; we can mirror snapshots to your buckets and use lifecycle rules; for DR we recommend regionally replicated buckets or cross-region replication per your RTO/RPO.
[08:03] Mark Dalton: any special networking for on-prem connections via VPN/Direct Connect? we have a colo with the clinical repo.
[08:11] Samira Khan: yes we support VPN/Direct Connect. For nodes in your VPC we can route traffic to on-prem via your existing VPN. For hosted PrivateLink, you'd route from your VPC to our endpoints — no extra internet.
[08:24] Jordan Lee: quick recap of customer's constraints to confirm: must not have outbound internet for inference nodes, KMS customer-managed, SOC2 compliance, prefer PrivateLink or in-account deployment, primary region us-east-1 with possible eu-west-1 replica, timeline pilot in March. is that right?
[08:40] Dr. Priya Rao: correct.
[08:43] Mark Dalton: yep.
[08:45] Jordan Lee: ok next steps — Jordan to send architecture doc + pricing, Samira to schedule infra deep dive, Silverpine to send CIDRs and network diagram. we'll propose pilot plan for a 3-node cluster and a benchmark run.
[08:59] Lena Ortiz: please include a network checklist and firewall rules.
[09:02] Samira Khan: will do.
[09:05] Dr. Priya Rao: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:07] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-caption errors; some product names may be mis-transcribed (e.g., PrivateLink vs Privatelink)
